candidates.rationale: High-ROE firms currently trading near the top of their own 63-day liquidity range draw sustained institutional flow-chasing, a quality x attention crowding effect.
Weekly trading volume accelerating relative to its own volatility baseline signals building participation ahead of full information diffusion, front-running continued price discovery.
A rising rate of change in daily volume (true second-derivative acceleration, not just an elevated level) marks the earliest stage of an attention shock, before it is fully reflected in price.

Volume that co-moves with the sign of returns (heavier turnover on down days than up days, or vice versa) reveals asymmetric, panic-driven participation, a liquidity-fragility signature that predicts short-horizon reversal.

A steep volume response per unit of return move (high volume-return beta) marks thin liquidity provision that is easily overwhelmed by order flow, embedding a liquidity-risk premium in subsequent returns.

A range skewed toward the day's high versus its low, independent of the day's net move, shows which side of the order book absorbed more flow intraday, an imbalance that predicts short-term continuation or fade on the thinner side.

The accrual anomaly is strongest where mispricing is hardest to arbitrage; pairing weak earnings quality with a persistently wide intraday range isolates the high-uncertainty names where that mispricing survives longest.

Stable, highly profitable firms whose trading-activity dispersion suddenly spikes relative to their own history are undergoing a liquidity/attention regime shift that typically precedes institutional re-rating flows.

Net signed dollar-volume flow (turnover on up days minus turnover on down days, as a share of total turnover) captures quiet accumulation or distribution pressure that runs ahead of the price move it eventually causes.

Trading volume near its own 126-day peak marks a liquidity/attention climax that typically exhausts and mean-reverts, while volume far below its peak indicates latent, unresolved attention that predicts a future re-rating.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Ratios with only $dollar_volume in the denominator risk collapsing into a proxy for dollar_volume itself: ABS(return)/dollar_volume was rejected for 0.90 correlation to a dollar_volume moving average. Give the numerator comparable dynamic range, or normalize the denominator too.
  2. Skip short-vs-long volume moving-average ratios (e.g. 5-day over 63-day); one such ratio failed the cheap screen (|t| 0.29). Same-window dispersion (std/mean at one lookback) is the pattern that actually passed (fitness 1.027).
  3. Don't graft a whole small fundamental subtree (e.g. RANK($roa)) onto an unrelated technical branch under one top operator. Two crossovers doing exactly that were rejected as sharing only 2 nodes with the fundamental parent, i.e. not a real fusion.
  4. Fundamental-technical fusions land better when both sides are normalized the same way: the one accepted mixed-niche entry ranked both branches (CS_RANK x TS_RANK), while the two rejected ROA crossovers combined a bare rank with a raw price ratio or an IF_ELSE gate.
  5. Volume correlated against a return-based term (ABS($return), or a 1-day volume delta) at a 21-day window gave this round's top two fitnesses (3.567, 2.616); the same idea against range ($high-$low) at 42 days failed the cheap screen. Keep pairing volume-correlation factors with return terms at ~21 days, not range terms at longer windows.
  6. Standalone $dollar_volume trend features (rank-drift, argmax, delta) failed the cheap screen in all 3 tries this round; this family only works interacted with a fundamental signal, as in the accepted accrual_gap x dollar_volume-delta factor.
  7. $asset_turnover combined with a 40-day return sum gave the two worst cheap-screen scores this round (0.09, 0.72); pair asset_turnover with other fundamentals or same-day range, not multi-week return sums.
  8. COUNT of days volume or range exceeds its own trailing mean carried almost no signal in both attempts this round; use the continuous ratio or z-score instead of a threshold count.
  9. Range-normalization factors ($high-$low over $dollar_volume, over $open, or via $low/$high min-max) each now have two neighboring windows tried (10&21, 63&126, 21&34); a window-only resubmission of these families will keep hitting archive_subtree or correlation, so change the core transform instead.
  10. Adding an outer TS_DECAY_LINEAR or CS_ZSCORE around an already-archived ratio or z-score expression still shares 9+ nodes with it (3 rejections this round); vary the inner computation, since wrappers alone don't decorrelate.
  11. The accrual_gap x dollar_volume and operating_margin/asset_turnover/leverage families already have close neighbors in the archive: a single added denominator or a rank-subtraction-to-ratio swap scored 0.84-0.86 correlation, not new signal. These need a different combinator, not an arithmetic tweak.
  12. A nested TS_DELTA(TS_MEAN(field,N),N) shape and an overnight-gap x range product (($open - DELAY($close or $high,1)) times ($high-$low)) both collided with alpha101 canonical subtrees regardless of field; avoid re-deriving these two shapes on a new field.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
Leave `parent_ids` empty and `changed_node` empty for EXPLORE.
